title: Conjecture 1.7 (Neumann Lara)
context_text: Neumann Lara introduced the dichromatic number in 1982 and proposed this conjecture as an analogue of Grötzsch's Theorem for directed graphs. The conjecture has been verified for planar oriented graphs on at most 26 vertices and holds for planar digraphs of digirth at least 4.
paper_contribution: The paper proves (Theorem 3.15) that if Conjecture 1.7 is false then S0-ORIENTED-2-DICOLOURABILITY is NP-complete, and notes that deciding whether a planar oriented graph is 2-dicolourable is NP-complete unless the conjecture holds.
paper_title: On the dichromatic number of surfaces

title: Problem 4.4
statement_text: What is the complexity of $\Sigma$-$k$-\textsc{Dicolourability} for $k \in \{4, 5\}$ and $\Sigma$ different from the sphere?
context_text: Surfaces are closed. A $k$-dicolouring of a digraph is a partition of its vertex set into $k$ sets each inducing an acyclic subdigraph; the dichromatic number $\vec{\chi}(D)$ is the least $k$ for which $D$ is $k$-dicolourable. Digraphs may contain digons (pairs of opposite arcs), so that $\chi(G)=\vec{\chi}(\overleftrightarrow{G})$ for the bidirected graph $\overleftrightarrow{G}$ obtained by replacing each edge by a digon; a digraph is embeddable on $\Sigma$ if its underlying graph is. For a fixed surface $\Sigma$, $\Sigma$-$k$-Dicolourability is the problem: given a digraph $D$ embeddable on $\Sigma$, is $D$ $k$-dicolourable? A digraph is $(k+1)$-dicritical if $\vec{\chi}(D)=k+1$ and every proper subdigraph has dichromatic number at most $k$. The authors prove that only finitely many $(k+1)$-dicritical digraphs embed on a given surface for $k\ge6$, so $\Sigma$-$k$-Dicolourability is polynomial-time solvable for $k\ge6$; they show $\Sigma$-$2$-Dicolourability is NP-complete for every surface (already for planar digraphs), and $\Sigma$-$3$-Dicolourability is NP-complete since planar $3$-colourability is. On the sphere, the cases $k=4,5$ are trivial since planar graphs are $4$-colourable. The undirected analogue (testing $4$-colourability of graphs on a fixed surface other than the sphere) is also open. Along with this, the authors also ask whether there are infinitely many $6$-dicritical digraphs embeddable on $\Sigma$, and separately the complexity of the restriction to oriented graphs with $k=2$.
